events.description: Estudio de Cuentos is held the last Tuesday of every month. Facilitation is entirely in Spanish. We recommend that at least one person in your group (child or caregiver) speaks Spanish. This program’s English-language version, Storytime Studio: Happy Halloween!, will be held Wednesday, October 28. SOBRE ESTUDIO DE CUENTOS Estudio de Cuentos ocurre el último martes de cada mes, a las 10 y 11 de la mañana, y está diseñado para niños desde recién nacidos hasta los 6 años y sus cuidadores. Los participantes son bienvenidos a nuestro estudio de arte para disfrutar de una hora especial de juego, lecturas en voz alta, y exploración artística. El programa es completamente en español , y se recomienda que por lo menos un miembro de su grupo (niño o cuidador) hable español. Estudio de Cuentos tiene cupo limitado. La entrada es por orden de llegada. ESTA SEMANA ¡Las Semanas del Espíritu de la Escuela de Arte llegan a su fin con el tema más divertido de todos: Halloween! Ven a Storytime con tu mejor disfraz de Halloween y acompáñanos en una búsqueda de fantasmas por las galerías, donde investigaremos quién—o qué—dejó las misteriosas huellas en la pintura Nómada (Nomad) (1988) de Annette Lemieux. Libro destacado: Gustavo, el fantasmita tímido por Flavia Z. Drago ANTES DE IR Estudio de Cuentos es una experiencia de una hora. Hay dos sesiones de Estudio de Cuentos con horas de entrada a las 10 y 11 de la mañana. La participación para cada adulto y niño está limitada a una hora. No es posible la preinscripción. La entrada a Estudio de Cuentos es por orden de llegada. Una vez que la sesión de las 10 de la mañana alcanza su capacidad, recibirás la opción de volver para la sesión a las 11 de la mañana. Estudio de Cuentos tiene capacidad limitada. Para garantizar una experiencia segura y agradable para todos, pararemos la entrada cuando ambas sesiones alcancen el cupo. Debido a el cupo limitado durante este programa público, pedimos que grupos escolares y otros grupos grandes de ocho personas o más (adultos y niños) , soliciten un programa privado, por favor contacte a HMSGEducation@si.edu . Todos son bienvenidos. Cuidadores lactantes son bienvenidos. Si hay servicios o acomodaciones que pueden mejorar su experiencia (por ejemplo, interpretación LSM, subtitulo en vivo, etc.), por favor escribe a HMSGEducation@si.edu . Agradecemos que nos envíen este tipo de solicitudes con al menos una o dos semanas de antelación. HORARIO DEL PROGRAMA Sesión #1 10 AM: Juego (fieltro, bloques, bosquejar) 10:15 AM: Lectura en voz alta 10:30 AM: Proyecto de arte 10:45 AM: Tour de galería Sesión #2 11 AM: Juego (fieltro, bloques, bosquejar) 11:15 AM: Lectura en voz alta 11:30 AM: Proyecto de arte 11:45 AM: Tour de galería Todos las sesiones se encuentran en la Escuela de Arte Hirshhorn en el nivel inferior del museo. El estacionamiento para cochecitos está disponible en el vestíbulo de Hirshhorn y en el nivel inferior. ABOUT ESTUDIO DE CUENTOS Held the last Tuesday of each month at 10 and 11 AM, Estudio de Cuentos is a program designed for kids from birth to age 6 and their caregivers. Visitors are welcomed into our studio to enjoy a special Storytime adventure of play, educator-led read-alouds, and art exploration. The entire program is facilitated in Spanish. We recommend that at least one person in your group (child or caregiver) speaks Spanish. Estudio de Cuentos has limited capacity. Entry is first-come, first-served. KNOW BEFORE YOU GO Storytime Studio is a one-hour experience. Two English-language Storytime sessions are held every Wednesday, with entry times at 10 and 11 AM. Participation for each adult and child is limited to one hour. Estudio de Cuentos, held the last Tuesday of each month at 10 and 11 AM, is a free Spanish-language edition of this program. No pre-registration is required. Entry is first-come, first-served. Once the 10 AM session reaches capacity, you’ll be given the option to return for entry to the 11 AM session until capacity is reached. Storytime Studio has limited capacity. We’ll pause further entry when both sessions reach full capacity to ensure a safe and enjoyable experience. Due to limited capacity during this public drop-in program, school, youth, and other large groups of eight or more (adults and children) are encouraged to reserve a group program by contacting HMSGEducation@si.edu . Everyone is welcome. Nursing caregivers are welcome. If there are services or accommodations that can improve your experience (e.g., ASL interpretation, live captioning, etc.), please contact HMSGEducation@si.edu . We appreciate receiving such requests at least one to two weeks in advance. events.name: History Film Forum presents "Creature from the Black Lagoon"
events.description: Join the History Film Forum at the National Museum of American History for a Halloween season screening of Creature from the Black Lagoon ! Originally filmed for the 3D technology of the 1950s, Creature from the Black Lagoon is a Universal monster movie removed from the castles and tombs of Dracula, Frankenstein, and the Mummy. Directed by Jack Arnold from a screenplay by Harry Essex and Arthur Ross, the film tells the story of a group of scientists who encounter an ancient amphibious humanoid creature while on an expedition to the Amazon. Richard Carlson and Julia Adams star, with Ben Chapman (on land) and Ricou Browning (in the water) sharing the film’s title role, a movie monster also known as the “Gill man.” Before the film, enjoy a rare opportunity to see the original costume gloves used for the “Gill man,” on view from the museum’s collections! This film has been rated G, or “General Audiences” by the MPA (Motion Picture Association). It contains depictions of mild peril and may not be appropriate for very young children. ______________ The National Museum of American History welcomes visitors of all ages and abilities. This event is wheelchair accessible. Captioning and assistive listening devices will be provided. Additional accommodations are available upon request; please email nmahprograms@si.edu . Seating is limited and reservations are recommended. Seating will be opened first to Eventbrite-registered attendees and then to walk-in visitors. When we reach maximum capacity, the event will be closed to the public. ______________ The History Film Forum is supported by the Golden Globe Foundation and Robert P. and Arlene R. Kogod Family Foundation. Technology upgrades in the Warner Bros. Theater were generously made possible by the Dolby family and Dolby Laboratories Inc.

events.name: Virtual Book Club | Martyr! by Kaveh Akbar
events.description: Register to join. Halloween costumes welcome~ Calling all readers! We’re starting a quarterly virtual book club, hosted by NPR’s Emily Kwong. You may recognize her from the hit podcast Inheriting about AAPI family history. Our club will meet once each season, with fresh recommendations from some of our favorite Asian-owned bookstores (including Loyalty Bookstore and Yu & Me Books). Expect: open-ended questions, organic conversation, and a structured activity. To kick off the club, our first book is Martyr! by Kaveh Akbar. Grab a copy from the museum store on your next visit. About Martyr! A newly sober, orphaned son of Iranian immigrants, guided by the voices of artists, poets, and kings, embarks on a remarkable search for a family secret that leads him to a terminally ill painter living out her final days in the Brooklyn Museum. Electrifying, funny, and wholly original, Kaveh Akbar’s debut novel is a paean to how we spend our lives seeking meaning—in faith, art, ourselves, others. Martyr! is a New York Times bestseller, National Book Award finalist, one of The New York Times Book Review ’s 10 Best Books of 2024, and a TIME Must-Read Book of 2024. “Kaveh Akbar is one of my favorite writers. Ever.“—Tommy Orange, Pulitzer Prize–nominated author of There There “ Martyr! is nothing short of miraculous.“— The New York Times Book Review Synopsis adapted from Penguin Random House. Content warning: This book is not suitable for younger audiences and includes explicit language, mentions of death, substance abuse, grief, war violence, and self-harm/suicide. Meet Your Host Emily Kwong Emily Kwong (she/her) is an NPR audio journalist working at the crossroads of history, science, and family memory. She is the host of two shows: Short Wave , NPR’s science podcast, and Inheriting , LAist’s show about Asian American and Pacific Islander families. Her reporting style is driven by empathy and context—rooted in a sense of people’s lives continuing on long after the story ends. Season 2 of Inheriting will debut in January 2027 and is about five families shaped by five immigration policies passed down through the generations. You can find her on Instagram @kwongsong. Emily loves to curl up with a good book and her orange cat Zuko. She’s very excited to host the first ever virtual book club for the National Museum of Asian Art. events.name: DC | Día de los Muertos (Day of the Dead)
events.description: Día de los Muertos (Day of the Dead) is a time for commemorating our ancestors. Rather than a period of mourning, it is an occasion for celebrating with family—both living and dead—and honoring the cycle of life. Enjoy family-friendly activities throughout the day, including dance performances by Grupo los Tecuanes, making paper marigolds to be placed on a Catrina statue, and making papel picado (perforated paper decorations) with David Amorozo. Learn how pan de muerto (bread of the dead) is made with Neil Vargas, Jr. Learn about La Catrina and her joyful view of life and mortality by interacting with live Catrinas roaming the festival. Visitors are invited to leave photos and mementos of their loved ones on the ofrenda (altar) or commemorate them by writing their names on a butterfly to attach to the memorial arch. SCHEDULE OF EVENTS LEVEL 3: imagiNATIONS Activity Center 10:30 AM | Story Time Families are invited to an interactive story time featuring the book Día de los Muertos by Roseanne Greenfield Thong. They will have the opportunity to engage with objects from the museum's Teaching Collection such as photographs, textiles, or natural materials to deepen their understanding of Día de los Muertos . Tickets may be needed to enter the imagiNATIONS Activity Center and Story Room. Please see staff at the Level 3 entrance desk for assistance. *Recommended for children ages 3-9 and their caregivers. 11 AM–1 PM, 2–4 PM | Hands On: La Catrina Creations! Celebrate the vibrant artistry of Día de los Muertos by decorating a plaster skull from a variety of La Catrina and Calavera (sugar skull) designs. Using paint markers, participants will create a unique keepsake to take home. LEVEL 1: Potomac Atrium 11 AM, 1 PM, 2:30 PM, and 4 PM | Dance Performances by Grupo los Tecuanes The name of the Danza de los Tecuanes (Dance of the Jaguar) is rooted in the Mixtec understanding of the duality of life and death and the fight of good against evil. The Danza de los Viejitos (Dance of the Old Men) is a humorous dance featuring dancers colorfully dressed as old men. The Flor de Piña (Pineapple Flower) is a folk dance from Oaxaca that features women dancing with pineapples balanced on their right shoulders throughout the routine. Each performance will offer bilingual narration. 11 AM-4 PM | Ongoing Activities Hands On: Paper Marigolds Marigolds, or cempasúchitl , serve a special purpose during Día de los Muertos celebrations. Their petals are used to create a path between the cemetery and the family home. Make your own tissue-paper marigold to take home or create a garland to adorn a nine-foot-tall La Catrina , the iconic skeleton fashionista that has become a symbol of Día de los Muertos. Alfombras de Aserrín (Sawdust Carpet) Display with Ubaldo Sanchez (Maya Mam) Found throughout Mexico and Guatemala, alfombras de Asserín were used in celebrations prior to contact with Europeans. Visitors will have intermittent opportunities to join artist Ubaldo Sanchez in creating a sawdust carpet. Demonstrations: Papel Picado with David Amorozo Papel picado is the Indigenous art form of hand-cut and die-cut paper banners that dates back to pre-Hispanic Mexico. The banners were originally made from a type of bark paper called amate . Today, papel picado is made by cutting tissue paper into intricate designs for Día de los Muertos and other celebrations throughout the year. Learn how it's made with demonstrations by artist David Amorozo. Demonstrations: Pan de muerto with Neil Vargas, Jr. Learn how pan de muerto (bread of the dead) is made with Neil Vargas, Jr., This round bread is traditionally eaten during Día de los Muertos , at a loved one’s gravesite or by the ofrenda. The bread is usually a soft, sweet, round bun often spiced with anise seeds, orange zest or orange flower water. Live: La Catrina La Catrina , the iconic skeleton fashionista that has become a symbol of Día de los Muertos shares a joyful view of life and mortality. Interact with live Catrinas throughout the day as they roam the festival. Butterfly Memorial Arch Select a butterfly of your choice, write a loved one’s name or a short message, and attach the butterfly to the memorial arch. Museum Ofrenda This temporary display honors those who have passed on with photographs or personal effects of the deceased accompanied by flowers, candles, religious icons, water, salt, and an array of food and drink.

events.name: Celebramos a los Veteranos: A Festival of Service and Remembrance
events.description: Across 250 years of American history, generations of Latinos have served the nation through the U.S. military. Presented by the National Museum of the American Latino at the National Museum of American History, the festival will explore stories of military service across generations—from Admiral David Glasgow Farragut to Colonel Marisol Chalas and veterans serving today. Visitors will also experience the music of military and civic life, exploring how marching bands, patriotic music and other musical traditions have become part of the American soundscape. A special story booth will invite veterans to record their own recollections of military service and reflect on why they served. events.name: DC | Service and Sacrifice: Veterans Day 2026
events.description: Join the National Museum of the American Indian in honoring the enduring and distinguished service of Native Americans in every branch of the US military. Throughout the day, visitors of all ages can learn more about Native military service and honor veterans through presentations, a short film, hands-on activities, various information tables, and more. The Native American Women Warriors (NAWW) will present the colors to begin the day's programming with a welcome from museum leadership. Take in the exhibition Why We Serve: Native Americans in the United States Armed Forces and watch the short film that complements the exhibition. Hear about the history and design of the National Native American Veterans Memorial on our grounds. Learn about the significance of tobacco in Indigenous cultures and make prayer ties to honor veterans. Meet with members of the Native American Women Warriors and learn about their service. Color your own Lakota star quilt as you learn about the history and significance of quilts in Plains cultures. Representatives from the Department of Veterans Affairs will be on hand to share information and resources available for veterans and their families. Dr. Christine Sims (Acoma Pueblo), Associate Professor in the Department of Language, Literacy, and Sociocultural Studies in the College of Education & Human Sciences at the University of New Mexico (UNM) will share the stories of Pueblo men who served as Code Talkers in World War II. Ryan S. Flahive , archivist at the Institute of American Indian Arts (IAIA), will discuss the life and legacy of Native fashion designer, co-founder of IAIA, and veteran Lloyd "Kiva" New (Cherokee. 1916-2002). The lighting of the flame of the National Native American Veterans Memorial will feature an Honor Song and drum by Dennis Zotigh (Kiowa/Isanti Dakota/Ohkay Owingeh Pueblo) and Ralph Zotigh (Kiowa/Isanti Dakota/Ohkay Owingeh Pueblo). The Native American Women Warriors will retire the colors to conclude the day's events. events.name: Pakeezah
events.description: New 4K Restoration! Following our Diwali celebration, enjoy this beloved Bollywood classic, a heartbreaking romance with gorgeous visuals and some of the most beautiful songs ever committed to film. Set against the backdrop of the courtly era of the Nawabs of Lucknow, Pakeezah is a poetically exquisite classic that took fourteen years to complete. The film’s painterly frames are saturated with color, opulent sets and costumes, haunting music, and actress Meena Kumari in an unforgettable performance. The courtesan Nargis is rejected by the family of her husband Shahabuddin and dies giving birth to her daughter Sahibjaan who grows up to become a renowned courtesan. But she lives in a gilded cage, yearning for love and a life of dignity. Her life takes a turn when a forest officer, Salim, accidentally encounters her while she is asleep in a train compartment. Captivated by her, he leaves behind a note praising her beauty and innocence without knowing her identity. Their paths cross again and they fall in love. However, misunderstandings and the stigma attached to Sahibjaan’s identity threaten to keep them apart. Description adapted from Film Heritage Foundation. Pakeezah was restored in 4K by Film Heritage Foundation at L’Immagine Ritrovata laboratory in association with Bilal Amrohi of Lionheart Cinema. Director: Kamal Amrohi. Country: India. Released: 1972. Length: 153 min. Format: DCP. Language: Urdu with English subtitles. Image courtesy of the Film Heritage Foundation

events.description: Seating is limited. Reserve your seat in advance to pick where you sit ($6 fee per order). Join the standby line for remaining seats on the day of the concert, free of charge. Pianist Eunbi Kim’s sonic memoir it feels like a dream features a soundworld of classical music threaded with an indie-pop awareness. Meanwhile, hypnotic projected visuals by new media artist Xuan expand the experience. This immersive multimedia performance explores questions of family and identity, offering listeners a space to meditate on the dreams they carry and pass on. it feels like a dream includes works by Daniel Bernard Roumain (DBR), Angélica Negrón, Pauchi Sasaki, and Sophia Jani for piano, pre-recorded voices, and electronics, written for and performed by Kim. The evening also premieres The Dreamers , a new work by Corey Chang written for Kim and commissioned by the Smithsonian’s National Museum of Asian Art. The work incorporates a poem that Kim’s father wrote more than thirty years ago, shortly after immigrating to the US from Korea—a meditation on the duality of hope and despondency experienced by immigrants navigating a new land. events.description: Fall in love with an evening of cinema and conversation. This Cinema + Conversation features a French-inspired dinner, a screening of Montmartre, and a conversation with the film’s writer and director, Leon Hendrix III, producer Maurice D. Hendrix, and stars Ito Aghayere and Jesse Williams. The evening begins at 5:30 pm with a French-inspired dinner, inviting guests to experience the flavors and atmosphere of France before journeying to Paris through the film. After dinner, guests will head to the Oprah Winfrey Theater for the 7:00 pm screening of Montmartre. Montmartre tells the story of a woman dissatisfied with her increasingly disconnected life; Jo travels to the storied Parisian neighborhood of Montmartre, where she meets Toussaint, a tour guide who loves poetry, magic, and romance. As the two grow closer, culture, art, and love intertwine, reconnecting Jo with a passion for life she thought she had lost. A moderated conversation will follow the screening with Leon, Maurice, Ito, and Jesse about the making of Montmartre and the film’s exploration of art, culture, place, romance, and rediscovery. Runtime: 1 hour, 43 minutes Rating: Not Rated (NR). Some material may be inappropriate for children under 13.

events.name: Brewing a Revolution: After Hours
events.description: Taverns and coffeehouses have always been more than places to enjoy a drink. As we celebrate the commemoration of America’s 250th anniversary, we’ll explore the role of taverns and coffeehouses as democratic spaces of civic life, hubs of economic development, and centers of regional and local identity. Join historians and industry experts for a conversation tracing the evolution of these social institutions and their influence on American culture, then taste history with five samples of historic and modern brews alongside small bites. Panelists: (Panel starts at 7:00 PM) Favio Garcia, brewery manager of Dynasty Brewing Company, Leesburg, Virginia Michelle Craig McDonald, historian, educator, and author of Coffee Nation: How One Commodity Transformed the Early United States Mike Stein, educator, brewer, author, historian, and cocreator of the research firm Lost Lagers Thor Cheston, cofounder of Right Proper Brewing Company, Washington, D.C. events.name: History in the Making: Carter G. Woodson Zine Lab
events.description: What happens when art meets history at the museum? Join artist Brittany Monet to make zines—small booklets that offer a creative way to tell a story or explore an idea. This hands-on, family-friendly workshop is inspired by the life and legacy of Carter G. Woodson, historian, educator, and longtime resident of DC’s Shaw neighborhood. Known as the “Father of Black History, Dr. Woodson worked with artists like Loïs Mailou Jones to publish illustrated books and journals about African American history for learners of all ages. At the time, Black history was seldom included in historical narratives. The program commemorates the 100th anniversary of Black History Month, founded by Dr. Woodson in 1926, and is offered in partnership with the Carter G. Woodson Home National Historic Site, National Park Service in honor of its grand reopening on November 7. Visitors can see books and journals by Dr. Woodson by visiting the museum’s current exhibition, We Make History, which explores stories of Washingtonians who work to improve our communities and those who record and share our history. History is in the making, and everyone can participate! Through history, art, and imagination, participants will leave with their own handmade zine and a deeper understanding of Carter G. Woodson’s legacy—and new ways of thinking about and making history!

events.name: Teen Studio: Cardboard Constructs
events.description: Teens: Ready to level up your art? Join us for Teen Studio, a free art-making program exclusively for teens ages 13–19. Push your artistic boundaries using materials and techniques inspired by artists whose work is now on view at the Hirshhorn. Dive into the Hirshhorn’s newly renovated Sculpture Garden with weekly workshops inspired by sculptures on view. This Saturday, think like artist Mark Grotjahn and create a work of art from discarded materials. Discover new ways to build with cardboard, inspired by the bronze sculpture Unti t led (Top and Exterior Gates, DeWalt Mask M33.e ) (2014). Drop in to Teen Studio every Saturday between 2:30 and 4:30 PM. Register for the entire school year here (one-time registration covers all sessions). Join one session or join them all! Meet in Art School on the Museum’s Lower Level. Looking for more? Explore Art School Everywhere , wherever you are, to learn about artists in the Hirshhorn collection and get creative any time. ABOUT TEEN STUDIO Teens ages 13–19 are invited to hang out and get creative at the Hirshhorn’s Teen Stu d io . Teen Studio is a free series of art-making workshops offered from 2:30 to 4:30 PM every Saturday. All skill levels are welcome—from the novice notebook doodler to the experienced teen artist, there’s something for everyone! Each month, we’ll dive into a fresh theme inspired by artists on view. Each workshop will offer a mix of time in the galleries, where we’ll encounter groundbreaking artists, and time in Hirshhorn Art School, where we’ll experiment with new media and materials. Whether you’re into painting, sculpture, printmaking, or something else, you’ll get hands-on experience and unlock new creative skills. If there are services or accommodations that can improve your experience (e.g., ASL interpretation, live captioning, etc.), please contact HMSGEducation@si.edu . We appreciate receiving such requests at least one to two weeks in advance.
